Case Study 02 · E-commerce · Meta

Zishta

1 Jan – 15 Sep 2026: ₹4,681,880 reported spend, 3,525 website purchases and ₹14,908,720 purchase conversion value. Calculated blended ROAS: 3.18×.

MetaE-commerce
ObjectiveDrive website purchases through structured sales and product-focused campaigns across Meta and Google.
Combined media scale₹6,410,709 total ad spend across Meta (₹4,681,880) and Google (₹1,728,829), 1 Jan – 15 Sep 2026.
Store performanceShopify: ₹38,027,688 gross sales, ₹33,532,190 net sales, 8,411 orders, 34.87% returning customer rate.
Blended ROAS5.23× — net store sales ÷ total ad spend across both platforms. This store-verified figure sits below the 3.18–9.94× platform-reported ROAS ranges, since it nets out discounts, reversals and shipping rather than counting attributed value alone.
How growth was achievedOrders eased slightly (-6% YoY) while gross sales still grew (+7%) — average order value rose. Google spend concentrated in Performance Max (~92%) for automated scale, while Meta ran dynamic catalog/DPA remarketing (the DSP_ campaign set) to keep the highest-value repeat segment converting. Growth here reads as efficiency and retention-led, not pure top-of-funnel expansion.
EvidenceMeta and Google campaign exports, platform screenshots, and Shopify Analytics store data.
LearningPlatform-reported ROAS and store-verified ROAS tell different stories — reconciling both against actual net sales gives a truer read of profitability than either alone.
Case Study 03 · E-commerce · Meta

Fitkin

1 Jan – 15 Sep 2026: ₹1,405,866 reported spend, 1,977 purchases and ₹4,631,981 purchase conversion value. Calculated ROAS: 3.29×.

MetaSales
ObjectiveDrive and scale e-commerce purchases through promotional, automated and catalog-based campaigns.
Combined media scale₹1,608,667 total ad spend across Meta (₹1,405,866) and Google (₹202,801), 1 Jan – 15 Sep 2026.
Store performanceShopify: ₹7,847,598 gross sales (+123% YoY), ₹5,586,509 net sales, 2,746 orders (+67% YoY), 35.05% returning customer rate.
Blended ROAS3.47× — net store sales ÷ total ad spend across both platforms, versus 3.29–4.46× on platform-reported figures.
How growth was achievedThe single largest campaign was a Meta Advantage+ sales campaign (₹565,619 spend, 1,183 purchases) — automated placement and audience expansion doing most of the heavy lifting. Discounts grew faster than sales (-304% YoY change), pointing to a deliberate offer-led acquisition push (BOGO, flash sales, EMV offers) layered on top of Google Performance Max for incremental reach. This is volume-led growth: new-customer acquisition at scale, financed partly through discounting.
Funnel evidenceMeta funnel data (purchases, checkouts initiated, adds to cart), Google campaign exports, and Shopify Analytics store data.
LearningRapid YoY growth financed by discounting needs the same scrutiny as spend — net sales and true blended ROAS matter more than gross sales growth alone.
Case Study 01 · Lead Generation · Meta

Lead Generation Account

Lead-result subset: ₹776,451 reported spend across 26 campaigns, producing 5,737 lead-result actions at a calculated weighted CPL of ₹135.

Lead GenMeta
ObjectiveGenerate leads and enquiries across multiple campaigns with different lead-result actions.
Scale20 campaigns are classified as lead-result campaigns in the supplied export.
Results5,737 reported lead-result actions across the subset.
EfficiencyWeighted CPL is ₹135, calculated from subset spend ÷ subset results.
AnalysisLead campaigns should be compared by volume, cost per result and objective definition.
LearningDo not compare lead results directly with purchase results because the conversion definitions differ.
